title: Be careful with "free trial" and "spin for sales"
body:
I'm glad that the people who like this app do, but it definitely is not for me. I like you can color code (I'm a nerd) but the color palette is limited and some colors are very close upon first glance. Making checklists and routines should be easier, especially since this is marketed towards those of us with adhd. Major flaw is you can only access routines on the day they are set up. If it's Monday and you want to go ahead and check off tasks that are assigned to Wednesday, a message pops up that says "let's concentrate on today" and other random messages.     If you want to rearrange tasks or the day you do them be prepared to delete your entire routine and start from scratch. 
You have to answer questions then agree to the free trial before you can even get into the app and play  around in it to see if you want it. I declined the free trial but then a wheel comes up with sale prices so I figured if I got a free month I would try it. I spun 50% off a year- I didn't want to commit to a year, but when I clicked the screen thinking I was  just moving past that point it "accepted the offer" and I was charged $20 right then. I made sure to go into subscriptions immediately and cancel the auto renewal. I can handle wasting $20, but I am very grateful I didn't waste $40.

title: Be Aware!
body:
I installed this app months ago just to check it out and see if it would really help me. However, I couldn't figure it out, and after playing with the app for a few hours, I got tired and decided to remove it. Then, a few days later, I noticed that I had been charged for a one-year premium plan without receiving any prior notification. I sent an email to the support team, explaining the situation and mentioning that I didn't have the app on my phone and had no knowledge of the upcoming payment. Their response was simply, "We are very sorry for the inconvenience, but there's nothing we can do. You can request a refund from the App Store!" Unfortunately, they did not provide a refund.

I'm mentioning this issue now because I've been searching for an app to help organize my life and came across this app again. Despite my previous negative experiences, I thought I would give it another try and see if it could be useful for me. However, just like the first time, it is not practical for me to use. It might be helpful for someone else, though, but it serves as a reminder of how unfairly they treated me.

If you also have ADHD, be cautious of falling into the same trap... if you know what I mean!!

title: ADHD and Depression helper
body:
I like using this app as a habit tracker. 

As someone with ADHD and depression, this app helps remind and motivate me to do basic tasks each day. I’m often terrible at remembering if I’ve taken my meds and this app has helped me stay consistent with taking them. When in a depressive episode, basic tasks like washing my face & brushing my teeth can fall to the wayside. This app helps motivate me & remind me to do those basic tasks. Being able to check off one small task like washing your face when in a depressive episode can feel like a huge accomplishment. 

My one pet peeve is that the widget does not refresh on its own. I also wish the data review for tracking habits was more user friendly and visually appealing like the “Habit” app. 

As for the other parts of the app, there are definitely flaws and room for improvement. There are typos in the quotes, the workouts don’t load, the alarm doesn’t always work, and the processes aren’t streamlined.

title: Great idea, but needs some improvements
body:
I have used the app for 3 days so far, and I really enjoy it. It offers different routines to pick and choose from, you can alter the details and add to do lists within the tasks you select. I also like they provide journals and wellness tutorials like stretches etc. It is very helpful to someone starting out in personal wellness.

My suggestions to improve the app:
- Allow back dated mood entries. My day typically ends around 10pm/11pm, so when I go to do my daily reflection it may be beyond midnight. This posts for the current day, not the day prior, and there is no way to adjust it, that I know of.
- Allow adjustments to future to do lists. I try to edit or adjust chores in the following days, and I get a purple bar that tells me to "focus on today". It is a bit annoying, and I tend to forget things easily (hence why I have this app) and that would be really beneficial to me if I could adjust things as I think about it, whether it be a day or a week from now. If there is a way to do this, it would be helpful to have an easier way of doing it.

Thank you for the app, I really appreciate the thoughtfulness that has gone into the apps creation and mood. The app is a very positive space and I look forward to using it as time goes on!

title: Amazing app only one complaint. Still worth it though

Cons:

When the alarm goes off it suddenly increases the volume of the speaker and you cannnnot turn it down until you complete your wake up tasks. title: Great app but need some updates
body:
Honestly I downloaded the app because I preferred the structure and theme compared to similar apps on the appstore and I’m glad I did download the app! To get most of the app you do need to subscribe to an annual subscription though but I believe it is worth it! There are many features available on the app that can’t be found in other similar apps such as a sleep tracker, sleeping aids (rain sounds in the background/ story audios/ etc), journals for several different topics, and gym/workout guides!:) 
I am quite happy with my experience so far but there needs to be some updates that maximise efficiency and just make sense.
1. If a habit repeats throughout the day, there needs to be the option to set several reminders/notifications for each periodic habit. 
2. There needs to either be a library of all habits created where you can go in and edit as you please, or enable users to go on other days of the week and edit their habits there instead of getting the alert “let’s focus on todays habit” that inhibits them from altering any habit that may not be a daily occurrence.
3. I find that notifications and reminders aren’t consistent. Some habits I get my daily notifications but others I don’t, I’m still trying to figure out why this is but if the creators can look into the issue that would be great! 
Overall I am pleased with this app and I do see the app does get consistent updates so I will stick with it and hopefully these issues will get resolved in due time :)

title: Best App I’ve Downloaded-ADHD Win!
body: Unlike countless other planner apps out there you don’t have to pay to actually be able to use the app. You wont believe how happy it makes me that you don’t need a subscription to be able to plan out your life. I personally find it disgusting and discouraging that loads of other apps take advantage of the challenges neurodivergent people face when they are just trying to make their life a bit easier and more organized. This app offers so many capabilities without having to pay. You can make checklists under activities and events. It gives you suggestions of things to add to your schedule. Events/activities are very customizable. It has a list of routines to try from hot spring to-dos to work out and cleaning routines. You can set alarms, track your sleep, listen to soundscapes and meditations, and check broadcasts. Broadcasts includes a great overview of how you slept including percentages of when you woke up during the night and when you were in light sleep and deep sleep. It also has sound recordings of your night. Weather in your area and fun history facts. They also give out free or discounted membership opportunities. It’s honestly a great experience and I feel more confident and in control of my schedule than ever before!

title: Limited and Profit-Driven
body:
The application is incredibly limited without a subscription, which is disappointing for those who may not have the financial means to purchase one.

Furthermore, the pre-created routines offered by the application are limited and not tailored to individual needs, which defeats the purpose of using such an app. Instead of providing a range of helpful and customizable routines, the application only offers a few basic routines that you can add to your plan AFTER you buy the subscription.

This approach not only limits the usefulness of the app, but it also seems to prioritize profit over the needs of the ADHD community. It is important to create an environment where individuals with ADHD can thrive, and an application that requires payment for basic features does not foster such an environment.

Overall, I would not recommend this application to anyone looking to improve their ADHD symptoms. With limited routines and a focus on profit, this app falls short of what is needed to support those with ADHD.

body: Having ADD I can truthfully say this is the best productivity app I’ve tried. So many others force you to create your routines, habits and schedules all by yourself. Most productivity apps start in a place of customization. By the time you figure out what schedule you want to choose, when you want to do it and how often you lose momentum it’s so exhausting you want to quit. The beauty of this app is that there are routine templates based on who you are and what you want to achieve and then you just add those goals/routines it to your custom one. Just the right amount of free choice but mixed so much with outlines that are pre-set you don’t have to figure a lot out. Definitely recommend - worth the hype. My only suggestion/request if possible would be to add a goal template that includes pets. When to walk them, spend time with them, take them to the vet, get them groomed. No points taken off though - this is awesome!

body:
I’ve been using this app for a few weeks, my mom is paying for my premium subscription and also has it on her phone.

The app is great, it’s been helping me keep track of my habits because I have ADHD and struggle with productivity, it also documents daily mood stats and reflections, every night I look forward to opening the app and checking off what I’ve done and reflecting on my day and documenting my mood. 

However I’ve had some issues, two days ago I opened the app and saw that all of my habits had disappeared and my habit stats disappeared too, I had to manually re-add all my habits and apparently my original habits aren’t completely gone because when I tried to re-add one of them it tells me that the habit already exists, but is nowhere to be found. My mood stats were untouched and still there, but that brings me to my next issue.

When it hits 12 am, you can’t go back to add your mood stat from the day before, you can go back on previous days in your habit stats to check off things you forgot to check off in the moment, but with mood stats you can’t do that, so if you forgot to document your mood for the day and it hits 12 then you’re out of luck. It’s my biggest pet peeve with this app, sometimes I don’t have the time/don’t remember to check things off immediately, it isn’t an issue with the habit stats but with mood stats you can’t do anything about it. 

Overall it’s a great app and I’ll continue using it despite its minor issues, I just hope my previously stated problem gets solved because my habits from the past 2 weeks are completely gone! (I saw a data repair button at the bottom of the profile tab, but when I clicked it nothing seemed to change so I’m not sure what that’s supposed to do)

title: April 2023 Update
body:
Purchased the app in January, lost all date in April and the Data Repair feature did not work. I’m going to add all my tasks back and give it one more go, I’ll update if it happens again. 

Overall, I still feel it is the best habit building widget. Streaks is a close second. Streaks allows you to choose which habits to include and you can have multiple widgets with different habits. 

If you aren’t looking to utilize the widget, I would pass on this app. They spend way too much time on the Discover tab and other tabs that I have a hard time believing anyone is using. The premade habits are mostly nonsense. Check them out during your free trial and you’ll see what I mean. The widget is what sets this app apart from others. 

Biggest areas for improvement (as of 4/23) are:

1. No good way to have a task be a certain amount of times per week or month without being day of the week specific. For example, maybe you want to exercise 5 times per week but don’t want to commit to certain days, or want to do something weather-dependent or once a month and it doesn’t matter the day. It would be amazing if there was a widget for daily tasks, another for weekly tasks, and another for monthly tasks.

2. You cannot backdate tasks, even by a day. This isn’t a huge deal but is annoying. Maybe you start a habit and it makes you feel good so the next day you add it as something to continue but you want to give yourself credit for doing it yesterday. You can’t. Also if you start something like “brush my teeth” as a habit midweek, in the widget it’s going to look like you just didn’t do that until midweek. Also wish it would let you pick which day of the week to start it on, or at least the option of starting the week on Monday. (It’s Sunday to Saturday.)

3. In the widget, if you only have a task set to a certain day, on that day, it will show in your widget and it will show like you didn’t do the task on the days it was not assigned. It needs to be shaded in. 

I feel like the type of people who would use this app long term are list makers and visual people and probably a lot of perfectionists and it would be a lot more motivating to continue use of those items were fixed.

title: Don’t fall for the one week trial. Try Reminders app first
body: I signed up for this app with a free week trial period hoping it would help me be more productive. I wasn’t really able to use it much that week, and since it was $40 to renew I planned on canceling. Well, not surprisingly, I forgot, because that’s something I do and why I was trying the app 😑. The day after the week trial, I contacted the company to ask if I could cancel, and be reimbursed partially, but got zero response. Not even a “no sorry we can’t do that”. Wasn’t happy about that, but figured I would work harder to use the app, and hope that I ended up liking it. After using it for a week, I don’t feel like it was that helpful. Setting up tasks takes way longer than it should, and YOU CAN’T MAKE A CUSTOM TASK. I take vitamins multiple times throughout the day, not at one single time, but I couldn’t make tasks for each of those, because you can only have one “take vitamins” task. Perhaps there is a way to create a custom task and I just didn’t find it? But if so, that is a problem - it should have been easy to figure that out if it existed. Creating and editing tasks was way more complicated than it needed to be. After becoming frustrated for those reasons, I thought maybe I can just do this through the Reminders app, and lo and behold I could, and it was much easier and simpler to use. And, it was easier to look at without all of the extra graphics and styling. Before you buy the subscription to this app, or even sign up for the free trial, do yourself a favor and JUST USE REMINDERS 🙄. You can set up weekly, monthly, biweekly, etc etc reminders. So much cleaner and simpler. 🤦🏻‍♀️🤦🏻‍♀️🤦🏻‍♀️

author: Josephwbeal

title: It’s just a checklist
body:
It’s just a checklist. This app offers nothing that iOS checklist can’t do; it’s just a library of routines— a lot of them basic— for basic people. 

I don’t pray. I don’t drink. I don’t drink coffee. I don’t have a sugar addiction. I just need help focusing. 

What does this app do? Put the buzzword “behavioral science” on— again— nothing more than a checklist. Behavioral science is about adjusting your choice architecture so that you go with the best options by default, or encouraging good habits with positive feedback. This app doesn’t do that at all. 

It’s just everything wrong with California apps:
Algeria art, royalty free stock photo testaments (believe these totally real people with no names!) to psych you up before you’ve even started, buzzwords, and— of course— a subscription fee because why not? Even though this isn’t a service, it’s just a checklist. 

Pass on this. It’s basic. It’s expensive. It’s empty. Go read about behavioral science from Richard Thaler, don’t believe these apps that have nothing to offer.

title: Hopefully more to come
body:
I think this is a fantastic app concept and I understand you are still in the process of building the app.

I just downloaded the app Saturday night and I am in my free trial to become a yearly paid subscription. So as I use the app more I will update my review.

Here are first impressions as I have only used a few features so far. (Tasks and alarm/sleep)

Things I love
-being able to create my own routines/tasks
-the ability to change colors and icons of tasks
-seeing my daily task list broken up between all day morning afternoon and evening tasks
-the alarm wake-up challenge (I have mine set to 3 math problems)
-nighttime listening

Things I’d like to see added
-the ability to set monthly/quarterly/yearly tasks opposed to just weekly
-the ability to alter a task set for a future day once it is saved
-the ability to rearrange my task list
-the ability to see a multi day list or monthly view of tasks
-the ability to set different alarm times for different days and in advance
-the ability to play nighttime sounds for longer periods, like a repeat 2, 3, or 4 times.
-longer recordings of noises while sleeping

I look forward to watching this app continue to get better.

title: I have some suggestions for improvement
body:
There are grammar errors all over the app from the broadcast talking in past tense when it should be present tense, to missing spaces or spelling errors. 

The app itself is more tedious than I thought it would be. I thought it would start as a guided process to help motivate me such as quizzes to find out what tasks would best for me and where to start based off my needs, but all the willpower had to come from me. 

The sleep tracking is not very accurate at all compared to others. I am okay with that as I know that wasn’t the main goal, but if you are gonna have it I would compare with Fitbit’s or Apple’s to see what kind of quality people expect. Some past apps I’ve tried allowed 3rd party apps which allowed me to use ones that I know work while still using the their app for everything else.

I would love to see a different medal system for each day. As someone with major depression, anxiety and adhd, many days my personal goal of how many to complete is 3 tasks maybe 5 even if have 30 tasks I want to track. It would be nice to be able to see the days I do super well versus the days I do one task. 

I do plan on getting the subscription as I think it’s a fair deal for other apps I have tried. With this in mind I do hope my review reaches the developers as these things will eventually need to be fixed if they want to keep me for multiple months/years.

title: A “self-care app” for the middle/upper class.
body:
We understand that small developers need to make money, but it's frustrating when they compromise the user experience by aggressively promoting discounts and subscriptions within the app's UI. These methods no longer work for today's generation of users, and it's disappointing to see a self-care app designed to help people grow and reach their full potential blocked by a paywall.

It's ironic that the only people who can afford to pay for this app are those who are already relatively stable in life and may only be using the app to maintain their status quo. The developers should consider alternative methods to encourage users to upgrade to the pro version. For example, they could offer purchasable in-app themes to customize the UI and make the app feel more cozy, warm, bubbly, or zen.

Locking mundane features that are free in other apps is pointless because users will simply switch to another app. It's time for developers to think outside the box and offer creative ways to enhance the user experience. It's frustrating to see potential wasted when developers continue to rely on outdated tactics. We hope to see more innovative ideas in the future.
At least the onboarding walkthrough was cute.

title: Love it
body:
I have adhd and it’s been pretty helpful so I got premium 

What I like:
* the fireworks animation 
* the days been marked silver or gold depending if you completed your habits 
* the ability to see track individual habits 
* other app functions: sleep tracker, meditations, workouts, etc. I’ve been able to delete a lot of other apps in favor of this one because it’s like a one stop shop. 

What I wish it had:
* more templates

For a user over 40 or so, it’s not as relevant as I’d hoped. For instance, I don’t need a daily reminder to shower, pray, or put on makeup. Nor do I need a tiny serotonin spike for checking those things off. 

Also, it is either impossible or too difficult to customize the daily goals. There may be a way to set up a goal of, say, walking a mile plus each day rather than “firming my butt,” but if it’s possible, it’s just too hard. I’m a retired software developer, and after noodling around for 30 minutes, I couldn’t figure it out. 

I had high hopes for this, but canceled the free trial after fully expecting to subscribe for the full year. I guess I’ll go back to my to-do spreadsheet, clunky as it is. Sorry guys

title: Limited Functionality, Too Many Pop-Ups
body: Jarring, to say the least, when I started using this app and couldn’t progress in my “self-care journey” without being assaulted by pop ups demanding I buy such and such and so on and so forth. There seems to be a bug where, no matter which page I tap on, I get an alarming pop up telling me that it’s my ONLY CHANCE FOR 35% OFF!! While I can understand smaller businesses/dev teams and do my best to support them where I may, the constant wailing of ads leaves a sour taste. Most apps (especially mental health apps) have small reminders notifying you of the benefits of purchasing a membership as opposed to staying free-to-use. Note: small. Infrequent, polite, understanding of their target audience. This, in stark contrast, feels garish and inappropriate. It’s a shame, because there is some good there, but it’s overshadowed by what feels distinctly of greed. I understand that the ads need to be present. But they’re entirely too much and it’s distracting from the main purpose of the app.
author: hexx__

title: Avoid if you have ADHD
body:
I downloaded this app to try it since there was postive reviews and it looked like it had endorsements. 

Initially I was put off by the set up steps but thought id see what the app was like anyway. The set up steps feel sort of condescending to someone with ADHD even when it seem like that is the intended audience. And also limiting - pick only one choice when multiple might fit. There were also typos in the set up steps and it seems like maybe this was translated, its like when you read Amazon product descriptions. 

Then I hit the paywall (by the way the premium option says “no payment now” but my phone still wanted me to authorize- maybe i would be charged later but I didnt want to risk it. ) I chose the cheap monthly payment,because again ADHD, i didnt want to forget to cancel later and I would accidentally pay $40 instead of $8. Then when I got in it was kind of condescending again and then provided me with what looked kind of like Pinterest schedule templates.  So then I went right ahead and deleted it. 

Sure it would be great if every day I did some kind of different exercise but come on is that realistic? And dont we get enough of this from Instagram? Just print out this cutesy little list and your life will ✨🌈 beeaauttifful and perfect 🌈✨ - come on 🙄. If youre going to have things to improve our lives please get them from verifiable reliable trained sources like therapists,social workers, researchers. And also, a growing movement for ADHD people is not to have self care piled on another “to do” or something else for us to achieve for us to be “normal” so it would be nice if the app reframed its view on self care to meet that.

Once you set a routine, there does not appear to be any way to alter it until the day it was set for. 

For instance- I was setting up routines for cleaning my house, intending to make each room its own day. I accidentally put my kitchen and bedroom both on Saturday, but since it’s only Tuesday, I cannot change it. This causes so much anxiety- I should be able to alter routines as needed, not just on the days they have been set for originally. 

Sadly this app will not work for me for this reason. It appears to be beautifully designed, just not very user friendly yet.

title: Good App, But There Are Some Issues
body:
The checklist that this app supplies are very useful since I can use just about all. Having a brief synopsis of the daily news is also very time efficient since I am almost too busy to have hours to read the news. And the sleep music and meditations are also helpful because I love having peaceful music to sleep by. 

However, I am about to cancel my premium subscription because I want to track my sleep. This part of the app doesn’t appear to be working properly. For one thing, it is stuck on two days ago. Today is April 14, but the data will only show for April 12.  I have attempted to reset it on the calendar but the calendar will not allow me to change the date. I am also concerned about the level of accuracy for my sleep tracking. It shows that I was awake for 2 hours the other night (I have no idea about last night or the night before because of the inability to change the date.) I really don’t think that I was awake that much because it isn’t supported by the “sounds” recordings.

title: Great App, but…
body:
I love this app and I cannot wait to see it evolve into something better eventually because it has so much potential. I accidentally got a year subscription after I forgot to cancel my sub but Im gonna stick with it for the year and edit this review as I go.

The thing that really irritates me most is how it disrupts my music if I have the app open at the same time as Spotify etc… It’ll just stop my music that I listen to throughout the day as im checking things off my daily routine. Really grinds my gears and if they fix it, I might renew next year.

I could go without the sleep report. Never use it tbh as its worthless to me IMO. I know how good my sleep is based off of how I feel when I wake up. Would rather not hear myself speaking latin in the middle of the night talking to demons and such…

The sleep sounds like rain/waves/stories are cool.

The routine editing/adding/removing function could be a little less clunky. And have more icons I guess.

title: Game Changer
body:
Truly helpful in a meaningful way
I suffer from insomnia and anxiety. I tend to overcompensate by being constantly “on” and trying to do everything perfectly. AlarmMe helps me remember to breathe, take moments and not over-schedule. It does this by allowing me to map out the things that are most important, creating an agenda, and giving me motivation, and guided meditations to deal with my anxiety. It really teaches me how to allocate time and effort to bring the most value in a short amount of time. Would definitely recommend this app to those who are overwhelmed by their work

title: Early to admit but this app is great so far
body:
I’m trying to manage a lot of new adjustments in my life and this app really helps sets a great tone for me. 
My mindset feels supported with the awesome tools they’ve set up on here and it’s worth it to strike a balance without having to sort out everything first, because with this app, they have a category for every daily/weekly/monthly duty there is, which you’d normally spend some time to figure out categories or even come up with categories on where to group your duties on your own. This can become discouraging and tiring to organise everything into its place, but this app clears all that for you, making you feel at ease knowing there’s a structure to follow. 

Get the app, it’s worth it. ✔️💯

title: App Feature Suggestions
body:
The app seems nice, I love the aesthetics 🫶🏾. However it would be awesome if there was an option to integrate your routine, tasks etc into your Google calendar or at least phone calendar to make the app more optimal and more useful🤔.

I’m not necessarily someone who likes using different apps that can perform somewhat of the same function, I like having things in one place without losing track of data and knowing that whatever update I do on the app will also reflect on my other calendars. This feature would be helpful ❤️ 

Otherwise the app is great✨!
